The strongest quantitative records are randomized-trial observation arms and surgical series; promote to directional language only if a qualified human finds an etiologic study attributing malnutrition to the syndrome rather than to tumor burden.
governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: weight loss and malnutrition in carcinoid-syndrome populations are documented in trial observation cohorts and surgical series, but the syndrome coexists with metastatic tumor burden, mesenteric fibrosis, and bowel obstruction that independently produce cachexia, and no identified study attributes malnutrition etiologically to the hormonal syndrome as opposed to the underlying disease process, so no directional claim beyond co-occurrence is supportable at the mapping level.

Tumor-confounder boundary recorded: the primary is the hormonal syndrome identity, not the underlying neuroendocrine malignancy; mesentericointestinal entrapment and metastatic disease are competing drivers of the same malnutrition outcome and are recorded as alternative etiologies rather than merged into the edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: In the TELESTAR randomized-trial population (metastatic neuroendocrine tumors with uncontrolled carcinoid syndrome), weight loss is described as associated with uncontrolled carcinoid syndrome and possibly with reduced survival, and biochemical nutritional markers (albumin, cholesterol) moved with weight change (Weickert 2018); pooled open-label extension data report that diarrhea- and flushing-driven weight loss accompanies the syndrome and that 68.7 percent of patients maintained or gained weight once syndrome control improved over 48 weeks (Srirajaskanthan 2021); surgical series of mid-gut carcinoid document severe malnutrition as a presenting feature of syndrome-bearing patients with mesenteric disease, and cachexia from mesentericointestinal entrapment accounted for 35 percent of deaths (Makridis 1990, 1997).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the trial analyses measure weight response to syndrome-directed therapy rather than attributing malnutrition etiologically to the syndrome, surgical-series malnutrition is inseparable from mesenteric fibrosis, obstruction, and metastatic burden, and protein-losing enteropathy, anorexia of chronic disease, and treatment effects are active competing drivers, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized hypersecretory-malabsorption pathway has been described: systemic serotonin and tachykinin excess in the carcinoid syndrome drive secretory diarrhea and flushing, and the resulting malabsorption, increased enteric losses, and anorexia would produce chronic negative energy and protein balance with weight loss and hypoalbuminemia; the observed weight gain and albumin rise when secretion is pharmacologically reduced (telotristat) is consistent with this pathway. However, reduced secretion also reduces tumor-drive diarrhea independent of any distinct syndrome effect, mesenteric disease independently obstructs and devascularizes bowel, and the trial data are treatment-response observations rather than etiologic measurements, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Malnutrition and weight loss co-occur with uncontrolled carcinoid syndrome in trial and surgical-series populations, but individual determination requires biochemically confirmed syndrome activity with chronology, anthropometric and laboratory documentation of malnutrition, exclusion of tumor-burden, obstruction, and treatment contributors, and review case by case by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Biochemical confirmation of syndrome activity (24-hour urinary 5-HIAA or chromogranin A) with chronology relative to the nutritional decline; serial weight, body-mass-index, albumin, and prealbumin records documenting malnutrition severity and trajectory; imaging and surgical records characterizing mesenteric and metastatic tumor burden and bowel obstruction; dietary and treatment history quantifying anorexia, diarrhea burden, and therapy effects; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Metastatic tumor burden and cancer anorexia-cachexia independent of the hormonal syndrome
Mesenteric fibrosis with bowel obstruction or ischemia driving intake and absorption failure
Treatment effects (somatostatin analogues, chemotherapy, surgical resections) on nutrition

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the quantitative evidence is treatment-response observation and surgical-series description, the hormonal syndrome is inseparable from metastatic disease as a malnutrition driver, and no etiologic attribution study exists; the edge records co-occurrence only and leaves every causal judgment to a qualified medical professional.

sourceReferences.citation: Weickert MO, Kaltsas G, Hörsch D, Lapuerta P, Pavel M, Valle JW, Caplin ME, Bergsland E, Kunz PL, Anthony LB, Grande E, Öberg K, Welin S, Lombard-Bohas C, Ramage JK, Kittur A, Yang QM, Kulke MH. Changes in weight associated with telotristat ethyl in the treatment of carcinoid syndrome. Clin Ther. 2018;40(6):952-962.e2. PMID 29724499. doi:10.1016/j.clinthera.2018.04.006.
sourceReferences.note: TELESTAR analysis (135 patients with uncontrolled carcinoid syndrome) reporting that weight loss is associated with uncontrolled syndrome and possibly reduced survival, with weight gain under syndrome-directed therapy accompanied by albumin and cholesterol rises; supports the syndrome-nutrition co-occurrence as a treatment-response observation, not an etiologic attribution.

sourceReferences.citation: Srirajaskanthan R, Pavel M, Kulke M, Clement D, Houchard A, Keeber L, Weickert MO. Weight maintenance up to 48 weeks in patients with carcinoid syndrome treated with telotristat ethyl: pooled data from the open-label extensions of the phase III clinical trials TELESTAR and TELECAST. Clin Ther. 2021;43(10):1779-1785. PMID 34598813. doi:10.1016/j.clinthera.2021.08.014.
sourceReferences.note: Pooled open-label extension (48 weeks) reporting syndrome diarrhea and flushing as drivers of weight loss with 68.7 percent of patients maintaining or gaining weight under therapy; documents the population-level weight-loss burden of uncontrolled syndrome at observational strength.

sourceReferences.citation: Makridis C, Ekbom A, Bring J, Rastad J, Juhlin C, Oberg K, Akerström G. Survival and daily physical activity in patients treated for advanced midgut carcinoid tumors. Surgery. 1997;122(6):1075-1082. PMID 9426422. doi:10.1016/s0039-6060(97)90211-7.
sourceReferences.note: Surgical series (121 patients) reporting substantial weight loss as a survival-reducing factor and malnutrition as a physical-activity impairment, while attributing 35 percent of deaths to cachexia from mesentericointestinal entrapment; supports co-occurrence and simultaneously documents the tumor-burden confounder recorded as an alternative etiology.
